sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.4% a year from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F201], but the path was a cycle rather than a straight line.

The first inflection was FY2017, when revenue rose 18.0% [D42] and operating margin jumped 6.8pp to 9.8% [F22][D52], helped by the absence of the FY2016 goodwill impairment and by higher sales volume [P66][P86].

FY2018 added another 20.4% of revenue [D92] and 5.3pp of operating margin to 15.2% [F23][D105], then FY2020 cut revenue 22.4% [D198] and margin 4.5pp to 10.9% [F25][D211] on lower end-user demand and dealer destocking [P59].

The recovery peaked in FY2023, with revenue up 12.8% [D357] and operating margin up 6.0pp to 19.3% [F28][D370] on favorable price realization and higher volume [P32][P31], before FY2025 gave back 3.7pp of margin to 16.5% [F30][D476] on tariff-driven manufacturing costs [P9].
Machinery, Power & Energy is 94.7% of revenue in FY2025 [D695] and contributed 4.0pp of the 4.3% revenue growth [D697][D463], while Financial Products added 0.3pp [D738].

Within the segments, Power & Energy grew 11.6% and contributed 5.2pp [D758][D759], led by Power Generation, up 32.5% and 3.9pp [D894][D895], while Construction Industries fell 1.6% and subtracted 0.6pp [D765][D766] and Resource Industries was flat [D779][D780].

The FY2025 top line rose on higher sales volume of $3.389 billion, partly offset by unfavorable price realization of $817 million [P13], with North America up 6% on higher equipment sales to end users [P12].

Profit did not keep pace: operating income fell 14.7% [D464] against revenue growth of 4.3% [D463], an incremental operating margin of -69.1% [D488], because operating costs grew 9.1% [D481] faster than revenue.
Over the window operating income compounded at 28.6% against 6.4% for revenue [F202][F201], so operating leverage was strongly positive across the cycle even though it reversed in FY2025.
Diluted EPS fell 14.7% in FY2025 [D467], in line with the 17.7% net income decline [D465], as the 3.5% share-count reduction [D483] cushioned but did not offset the profit drop.
Operating margin of 16.5% in FY2025 [F30] sits above the window median of 14.3% [D1123] but below the FY2024 high of 20.2% [D1122] and well above the FY2016 low of 3.0% [D1121].
The FY2025 bridge is almost entirely cost of revenue, which cost 4.2pp of margin as it rose to 66.2% of revenue [D490][D441], while SG&A and R&D were roughly neutral [D492][D491].

Operating profit fell $1.921 billion primarily on unfavorable manufacturing costs of $2.148 billion and unfavorable price realization of $817 million, partly offset by the profit impact of higher sales volume of $1.218 billion, with manufacturing costs largely reflecting higher tariffs [P9].

The largest positive move in the window was FY2023, when cost of revenue added 5.8pp of margin as it fell to 63.8% of revenue [D384][D335], driven by favorable price realization and higher sales volume [P31].
Below the line, the effective tax rate rose to 24.0% in FY2025 [D449] from 19.7% [D396], so net margin of 13.1% [F50] fell 3.5pp [D477], slightly less than the 3.7pp operating-margin decline [D476].
Operating cash flow of $11.7 billion [F80] was 1.32x net income [D450] and free cash flow of $8.9 billion [F100] was 1.00x [D451], against a window median free-cash-flow conversion of 0.96x [D1135].

Free-cash-flow margin of 13.2% [D447] is above the window median of 11.9% [D1129] but below the FY2023 high of 16.8% [D1128], and capital intensity has risen: capex reached 4.2% of revenue [D446] and 1.25x D&A [D452] in FY2025.

Machinery, Power & Energy operating cash flow rose to $12.278 billion from $11.437 billion primarily on lower working capital requirements and lower cash taxes paid, partly offset by lower profit before taxes [P4].

The capex step-up is visible in the 41.9% increase in capital expenditures to $2.821 billion [D470][F90], which with higher receivables and inventory [D486][D487] explains the 11.2% fall in free cash flow [D469].
The company is in net debt of $26.2 billion [D456], or 38.8% of revenue [D457], after net cash fell for a second year from $22.1 billion in FY2023 [D350] through $24.9 billion in FY2024 [D403].

That net-debt ratio is better than the industrials peer median of -35.6% of revenue but only the 43rd percentile of the seven-peer group [D1152][D1151], and the current ratio of 1.44x [F180] is above its window median of 1.40x [D1138].
Total debt rose 14.1% to $36.2 billion [D485][D455] while cash rose 44.9% to $10.0 billion [D484][F140], so the net-debt increase was modest relative to the gross move.
Free cash flow funded $7.9 billion of buybacks and dividends in FY2025 [D458], 89.0% of free cash flow [D459], and the diluted share count fell 3.5% [D483].
Return on average equity of 43.5% [D462] ranks at the 100th percentile of the six-peer group against a 23.3% median [D1155][D1156], reflecting both strong earnings and a leveraged balance sheet.

Net debt has now widened two years running, from $22.1 billion in FY2023 [D350] to $26.2 billion in FY2025 [D456], as buybacks and dividends of 89.0% of free cash flow [D459] and rising capex outran cash generation; the leverage is manageable but leaves less room if the tariff cost pressure persists [R1].

The FY2025 margin reversal is the more consequential flag: operating margin fell 3.7pp [D476] on tariff-driven manufacturing costs [P9], and the FY2026 outlook still anticipates higher manufacturing costs across segments [P14], so the FY2024 peak of 20.2% [D1122] may not be quickly recovered.
Revenue declined 3.4% in FY2024 [D410] on lower equipment sales to end users [P22], a one-year dip that reversed with 4.3% growth in FY2025 [D463] [R2].

Net income for FY2021 to FY2025 in the table comes from the proxy pay-versus-performance table rather than the 10-K and differs by up to 0.06% [R3][F40][X20]; the 10-K figure for FY2025 is $8.882 billion [X20], so precision-sensitive comparisons should use that.

Operating margin: a FY2026 reading back above the FY2024 high of 20.2% [D1122] would confirm the tariff hit was transitory, while a move below the 14.3% window median [D1123] would signal the cost pressure is structural; it appears in the FY2026 10-K.

Cost of revenue as a share of revenue: a fall back toward the FY2024 level of 62.0% [D388] would confirm margin recovery, while a rise above the FY2025 level of 66.2% [D441] would extend the compression.

Free cash flow: a recovery above the FY2023 high of $11.3 billion [F98] would confirm the capex cycle is peaking, while a fall below the FY2025 level of $8.9 billion [F100] would pressure the buyback and dividend programme that consumed 89.0% of free cash flow [D459].

Net cash: a further widening of net debt beyond the FY2025 level of $26.2 billion [D456] would confirm the balance-sheet trend, while a return toward the FY2023 level of $22.1 billion [D350] would reverse it.
